newsitem.title: UK: Rocco Forte to return with Cardiff hotel.
newsitem.headline: Rocco Forte to return with Cardiff hotel.

text.p: Sir Rocco Forte is set for a return to the hotel business with a 12 million stg luxury development on the Cardiff Bay waterfront in south Wales.

The 120-bed hotel, which is expected to open in time for the 1999 Rugby Union World Cup in Wales, signals Sir Rocco's return to the industry after he lost control of the Forte empire to Granada Group Plc earlier this year.

"We are actively examining a number of luxury hotel projects throughout Europe at present," Sir Rocco said. "Within the UK, I believe that there is a particular opportunity in several fast growing locations, such as Cardiff Bay, to add hotels which are a cut above the existing provision."

Sir Rocco aims to build a chain of 20 to 50 luxury hotels across the UK and Europe over the next five years, some owned and some under management contracts. They will be grouped under the Rocco Forte Hotels brand.
Forte has made no secret of his desire to reenter the hotel market after losing the business which his father had founded in the 1930s as a central London milk bar.
He had attempted to buy a number of the luxury Forte hotels which Granada is planning to sell but failed to agree a deal.
